about: Seed of the Public Safety Data Resources directory (Admin → Safety data resources). Each entry was checked against its official page on the date in verified; entries with verified null are drafts awaiting an editor. Inclusion here never enables collection: that is data_sources only.

resources.name: Canada Vigilance Adverse Reaction Online Database
resources.purpose: Which suspected adverse reactions to health products have been reported in Canada?

coverage.products: Health products; vaccines since 1 January 2011; blood and blood components since 1 September 2015
coverage.reportTypes: Voluntary reports from consumers and health professionals; mandatory reports from manufacturers and distributors
coverage.years: 1965 to date (data to 31 May 2026 at the check)

access.note: Online search, plus the full data set as monthly compressed ASCII files (about 344 MB) for loading into your own database.

reuse.note: Not stated on the page checked.

resources.limitations: Health Canada says the database should not be used on its own to evaluate a product's safety, as it does not provide conclusive information.

resources.name: European database of suspected adverse drug reaction reports (adrreports.eu)
resources.purpose: Which suspected side effects have been reported in the EEA for a medicine or active substance?

coverage.products: Authorised medicines and vaccines (centrally authorised by name or substance; others by substance only)
coverage.reportTypes: Spontaneous suspected adverse reaction reports

access.note: The public sees a restricted set of data elements after accepting a disclaimer. Marketing authorisation holders, regulators and academics get more under the EudraVigilance access policy, with registration.

reuse.note: May be reproduced for non-commercial and commercial purposes, provided EMA is acknowledged as the source.

resources.limitations: EMA says the data do not confirm a link between the medicine and the effect and should not be used to judge how likely a side effect is.

resources.name: FDA Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS) Public Dashboard and quarterly data files
resources.purpose: Which suspected adverse events, medication errors and quality complaints have been reported to FDA for a drug?

coverage.countries: United States, plus reports FDA receives from other countries
coverage.reportTypes: Adverse event reports, medication error reports, product quality complaints resulting in adverse events
coverage.years: Quarterly data files from 2004 Q1; the dashboard covers earlier years

access.note: Public Dashboard for search; non-cumulative quarterly ASCII or XML zip files for analysis. The same data is in openFDA's API. FDA now also calls this the Adverse Event Monitoring System (AEMS).

reuse.note: Not stated on the pages checked; openFDA publishes FAERS data under CC0.

resources.limitations: Spontaneous reports: a report does not show the drug caused the event, reports are duplicated and under-reported, and counts cannot give incidence. FDA notes the raw files need relational-database skills.

resources.name: JADER: Japanese Adverse Drug Event Report database
resources.purpose: Which suspected adverse drug reactions have been reported in Japan, as data I can analyse?

coverage.reportTypes: Line listings of suspected adverse reaction case reports, with CSV data
coverage.years: Not stated on the terms page

access.note: Free CSV download after accepting the terms of use. Pages are in Japanese. PMDA supplies no analysis tools.

reuse.note: Free to use under PMDA's terms: cite JADER in publications, credit PMDA in services built on it, pass the terms on to secondary users, and report health hazards found to PMDA.

resources.limitations: PMDA asks users to understand ICH E2B before use and accepts no liability; use is at the user's own judgement. Spontaneous reports do not show causation.

resources.name: MAUDE: Manufacturer and User Facility Device Experience
resources.purpose: What device malfunctions, injuries and deaths have been reported to FDA for a medical device?

coverage.reportTypes: Mandatory reports (manufacturers, importers, user facilities) and voluntary reports
coverage.years: Search: last 10 years. Data files: voluntary reports since 1993, manufacturer reports since 1996

access.note: Search is capped at 500 results; zipped data files updated monthly. Device events are also in openFDA. FDA plans to move MAUDE data into AEMS in 2026.

reuse.note: Not stated on the pages checked.

resources.limitations: FDA says an event report does not mean there is a problem with the device and the data cannot be used to work out event rates; trade secrets and reporter identities are removed.

resources.name: Medsafe Suspected Medicine Adverse Reaction Search (SMARS)
resources.organization: Medsafe, New Zealand Ministry of Health
resources.purpose: Which suspected adverse reactions have been reported in New Zealand for a medicine?

coverage.reportTypes: Reports to the Centre for Adverse Reactions Monitoring

access.note: Not yet checked.

reuse.note: Not yet checked.

resources.limitations: Not yet checked: the search page was found from Medsafe's reporting page but has not been read.

resources.name: MHRA Yellow Card interactive Drug Analysis Profiles (iDAPs)
resources.organization: Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (UK)
resources.purpose: Which suspected adverse reactions have been reported in the UK for an active substance or vaccine?

coverage.reportTypes: All suspected adverse reactions reported through the Yellow Card scheme
coverage.years: Not stated; about a one-month delay

access.note: Interactive profile per substance. Device reports are collected but not published as profiles.

reuse.note: Not stated on the pages checked.

resources.limitations: MHRA asks readers to use the guidance at the bottom of each profile to avoid misinterpreting the data; reports do not prove causation.

resources.name: openFDA APIs
resources.purpose: How can I query FDA adverse event, recall and labeling data programmatically?

coverage.reportTypes: Adverse events, recall enforcement reports, drug labels and other FDA data sets

access.note: Works without a key at lower limits (1,000 requests a day); a free key raises it to 120,000 a day.

reuse.note: Public domain under CC0 1.0, except GMDN device terms, which need a licence from the GMDN Agency for commercial use.

resources.limitations: openFDA says not all data has been validated for clinical or production use. Adverse event records carry the same cautions as FAERS and MAUDE.

resources.name: TGA Database of Adverse Event Notifications (DAEN)
resources.purpose: Which adverse events have been reported in Australia for a medicine, vaccine or device?

coverage.reportTypes: Adverse event notifications

access.note: Not yet checked: the site's terms page now sits on aems.tga.gov.au.

reuse.note: Not yet checked.

resources.limitations: Not yet checked: TGA blocks automated reading of the DAEN pages, so an editor needs to verify this entry.

resources.name: Vaccine Adverse Event Reporting System (VAERS) data and CDC WONDER search
resources.organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention and US Food and Drug Administration
resources.purpose: Which adverse events after vaccination have been reported in the US for a vaccine?

coverage.countries: United States (US-licensed vaccines, including some foreign reports)
coverage.reportTypes: Spontaneous reports from anyone; secondary reports added from May 2025
coverage.years: 1990 to date; de-identified data appear 4 to 6 weeks after receipt

access.note: Raw CSV downloads at vaers.hhs.gov and the CDC WONDER query tool. Public data hold initial reports only, not follow-up.

reuse.note: CDC WONDER data use restrictions: statistical reporting and analysis only, and no attempt to identify anyone.

resources.limitations: CDC and FDA state that report numbers alone cannot show a vaccine caused an event; reports may be incomplete, coincidental or unverified, and VAERS is passive and under-reports.

resources.name: VigiAccess (WHO global database VigiBase)
resources.organization: Uppsala Monitoring Centre for the WHO Programme for International Drug Monitoring
resources.purpose: How many suspected adverse reactions have been reported worldwide for a medicine or vaccine, and of what kind?

coverage.reportTypes: Summarised individual case safety reports in VigiBase (over 40 million reports)

access.note: VigiAccess gives limited statistics openly. Full VigiBase data is free to WHO Programme members and available for a fee to companies, software providers and researchers. UMC lists a VigiAccess API for developers (not checked).

reuse.note: Not stated on the pages checked.

resources.limitations: UMC says analysis and interpretation of VigiBase data requires specialised knowledge. Counts reflect reporting, not incidence or causality. Details checked on UMC's data access pages; the VigiAccess site itself needs JavaScript and was not read.

resources.name: EMA Direct healthcare professional communications (DHPCs)
resources.purpose: Which important safety letters have been sent to EU healthcare professionals about a medicine?

coverage.countries: EU and EEA, with links to each national register
coverage.reportTypes: DHPCs sent by marketing authorisation holders about important new safety information

access.note: EU-level DHPCs via EMA's medicine search and the DHPC table in Download medicine data; national registers are linked by country.

reuse.note: Not stated on the page checked.

resources.limitations: EMA notes national authorities may adapt the EU text, so the letter a professional receives may differ; national registers may not be in English. Shortage letters are published separately.

resources.name: EMA PRAC meeting highlights and safety signal recommendations
resources.organization: European Medicines Agency (Pharmacovigilance Risk Assessment Committee)
resources.purpose: What safety signals and risks has the EU safety committee assessed, and what product information changes did it recommend?

coverage.products: Human medicines, centrally and nationally authorised
coverage.reportTypes: PRAC agendas, minutes, meeting highlights; monthly recommendations on safety signals with new product information wording
coverage.years: Signal recommendations since September 2012; meeting documents in a paged archive

access.note: Documents are PDFs; new product information wording is given in English and other EU languages. RSS available.

reuse.note: No reuse terms on the pages checked.

resources.limitations: EMA notes that the presence of a safety signal does not mean the medicine caused the reported adverse event. Recommendations still need adoption before the label changes.

resources.name: FDA Drug Safety Communications
resources.purpose: What new safety issues has FDA communicated to patients and health professionals about a medicine?

coverage.reportTypes: Drug Safety Communications
coverage.years: 2020 to date on the page; earlier communications in an archived copy linked from the page

access.note: Dated web list; email alerts available.

reuse.note: No reuse terms on the page checked.

resources.limitations: Covers only the issues FDA chose to communicate this way; label changes and other actions may be published elsewhere (Drugs@FDA, DailyMed).

resources.name: FDA Recalls, Market Withdrawals and Safety Alerts, and the Enforcement Report
resources.purpose: Has a product been recalled or withdrawn in the US, why, and how serious is the recall?

coverage.products: Drugs, biologics, medical devices, and other FDA-regulated products
coverage.reportTypes: Recall press releases and public notices; Enforcement Report recall records with recall class
coverage.years: Recalls page: about the last three years, then archived. Enforcement Report: from 8 June 2012

access.note: Recalls page has filters and an XLSX download. The Enforcement Report has search, CSV export and a documented API.

reuse.note: No reuse terms on the pages checked.

resources.limitations: FDA says not all recalls have press releases or appear on the recalls page; use the Enforcement Report for a more complete listing.

resources.name: Government of Canada Recalls and safety alerts
resources.purpose: Has a health product been recalled in Canada, or has Health Canada issued a safety alert?

coverage.products: Health products (drugs, devices, natural health products) plus food, consumer products and vehicles
coverage.reportTypes: Recalls, safety alerts, advisories
coverage.years: Active and archived records (about 34,000 at the check)

access.note: Recall and alert data in CSV and JSON on the Open Government Portal, updated daily; RSS and email.

reuse.note: The open data set is published on the Open Government Portal; check its licence. Website terms at canada.ca/en/transparency/terms.

resources.limitations: The database mixes health products with food and consumer products; filter by category.

resources.name: MHRA alerts, recalls and safety information: medicines and medical devices
resources.organization: Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (UK)
resources.purpose: Is there a UK recall, field safety notice or patient safety alert for a medicine or device?

coverage.reportTypes: Medicines recalls and defect notifications (with class), field safety notices, national patient safety alerts, device safety information
coverage.years: Searchable archive (about 1,460 messages at the check)

access.note: Filters by message type, specialty and date; email alerts and an Atom feed.

reuse.note: GOV.UK content is available under the Open Government Licence v3.0, except where otherwise stated.

resources.limitations: Field safety notices are written by manufacturers; MHRA lists them but the content is the manufacturer's.

resources.name: MHRA Drug Safety Update
resources.organization: Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (UK)
resources.purpose: What safety advice has the UK regulator issued to health professionals about a medicine?

coverage.reportTypes: Drug Safety Update articles; monthly summaries of letters and medicine recalls sent to health professionals
coverage.years: Searchable archive (about 870 articles at the check)

access.note: Search with therapeutic-area and date filters; email alerts and an Atom feed.

reuse.note: GOV.UK content is available under the Open Government Licence v3.0, except where otherwise stated.

resources.limitations: Advice reflects UK licensing and practice and may differ from other countries.

resources.name: PMDA Safety Information Regarding Drugs (English) and Revisions of Precautions
resources.organization: Pharmaceuticals and Medical Devices Agency (Japan), with MHLW
resources.purpose: What safety measures and package-insert precaution revisions has Japan issued for a drug?

coverage.reportTypes: Revisions of PRECAUTIONS (MHLW notices and PMDA summaries), Yellow and Blue Letters, PMDA Risk Communications, Alerts for Proper Use, RMPs
coverage.years: Revisions of Precautions in English: FY2014 to date

access.note: Year-by-year pages with documents.

reuse.note: PMDA pages carry 'All Rights Reserved' with no reuse licence.

resources.limitations: PMDA warns the English site may be inaccurate due to machine translation and attached files are not translated; the Japanese pages are authoritative.

resources.name: TGA safety alerts and Database of Recalls, Product Alerts and Product Corrections (DRAC)
resources.purpose: Is there an Australian safety alert, recall or product correction for a medicine, biological or device?

coverage.reportTypes: Safety alerts and advisories; recalls, product alerts, product corrections with hazard class

access.note: DRAC search by product, ingredient, ARTG number, date and action type (needs JavaScript).

reuse.note: TGA states copyright restrictions apply to DRAC; see the TGA website copyright page.

resources.limitations: TGA says an alert doesn't always mean the product is unsafe, and does not guarantee DRAC is complete or current. Actions appear two days after the decision.

resources.name: WHO Medical Product Alerts
resources.purpose: Has WHO warned about a falsified or substandard medicine, vaccine or diagnostic?

coverage.products: Medicines, vaccines and in vitro diagnostics
coverage.reportTypes: Medical Product Alerts on substandard and falsified products; information notices

access.note: Dated web list linking to each alert.

reuse.note: WHO website terms of use apply (acknowledge WHO; no commercial use without permission).

resources.limitations: Covers alerts WHO received and confirmed; absence of an alert does not mean a product is genuine.

resources.name: Australian Register of Therapeutic Goods (ARTG) search
resources.purpose: Can a medicine, biological or device be supplied in Australia, and what are its Product Information and Consumer Medicine Information?

coverage.reportTypes: ARTG entries with sponsor and manufacturer, PI and CMI documents

access.note: Search by name, ID or sponsor; a visualisation tool offers advanced search.

reuse.note: Not stated on the page checked.

resources.limitations: TGA notes not all CMI and PI documents are available.

resources.name: DailyMed
resources.purpose: What does the current US label (prescribing information, patient labeling, carton) say?

coverage.products: Prescription and biological drugs, nonprescription drugs, certain medical devices, medical gases, animal drugs
coverage.reportTypes: Structured Product Labeling (SPL) as submitted to FDA
coverage.years: Current labeling in use; daily, weekly and monthly update files

access.note: Full and incremental SPL zip downloads; REST web services (JSON or XML), no registration stated.

reuse.note: Not stated on the pages checked; see the NLM copyright page.

resources.limitations: NLM says 'in use' labeling may not match the most recent FDA-approved labeling in Drugs@FDA, and NLM does not review SPL content before publication.

resources.name: Drugs@FDA
resources.purpose: When was a drug approved in the US, and what labeling and reviews did FDA approve?

coverage.products: Drugs and CDER-regulated biologics approved for human use (not CBER products such as vaccines and blood products)
coverage.reportTypes: Approval history, approved labeling, FDA reviews, monthly approval reports
coverage.years: Historical approvals; data file updated each weekday

access.note: Drugs@FDA data file: zip of tab-delimited tables, updated Monday to Friday.

reuse.note: Not stated on the pages checked.

resources.limitations: Excludes CBER-regulated products (vaccines, blood products, cell and gene therapies).

resources.name: EMA medicines (EPARs and product information) and medicine data tables
resources.purpose: What is the current EU product information and assessment history for a centrally authorised medicine?

coverage.products: Centrally authorised human and veterinary medicines; herbal products
coverage.reportTypes: EPARs, product information, post-authorisation procedures, referrals, PSUSAs, DHPCs, shortages

access.note: Excel tables updated overnight, and JSON data files for the website.

reuse.note: Not stated on the pages checked.

resources.limitations: Only medicines evaluated by EMA; nationally authorised medicines are in national registers.

resources.name: Health Canada Drug Product Database (DPD)
resources.purpose: Is a drug approved or marketed in Canada, and what is its product monograph?

coverage.products: Human pharmaceutical and biological drugs, veterinary drugs, radiopharmaceuticals, disinfectants (about 47,000 products)
coverage.reportTypes: Product details, status, product monographs
coverage.years: Approved, marketed, dormant and cancelled products

access.note: Data extracts and a JSON/XML API; updated nightly.

reuse.note: No licence stated on the pages checked; Canada.ca terms and conditions apply.

resources.limitations: Health Canada does not provide medical advice through the database; some product types may appear with a delay.

resources.name: LiverTox
resources.organization: National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases (NIH), on NCBI Bookshelf
resources.purpose: How often and how does a drug or supplement cause liver injury, and how is it managed?

coverage.products: Prescription and nonprescription drugs, selected herbal and dietary supplements
coverage.reportTypes: Drug records on liver injury with references and case reports

access.note: Free on NCBI Bookshelf.

reuse.note: LiverTox is copyright free; acknowledgement is requested when used in publications.

resources.limitations: A clinical reference summarising literature, not a reporting database; check each record's update date.

resources.name: MHRA Products (SPCs, leaflets and assessment reports)
resources.organization: Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (UK)
resources.purpose: What do the UK SPC and patient leaflet for a medicine currently say?

coverage.reportTypes: Summaries of Product Characteristics, patient information leaflets, Public Assessment Reports
coverage.years: PARs for authorisations granted after 30 October 2005

access.note: Search by name or PL number; A to Z by substance.

reuse.note: Not stated on the page checked.

resources.limitations: Documents follow each product's licence history; check the date on each document.

resources.name: PMDA prescription drug package insert search
resources.purpose: What does the current Japanese package insert, RMP or interview form say for a drug?

coverage.reportTypes: Package inserts, patient drug guides, interview forms, RMPs, review reports, safety bulletins, DSU

access.note: Search by name, therapeutic class or any package-insert section, including adverse reactions.

reuse.note: Copyright PMDA, All Rights Reserved; no reuse licence stated.

resources.limitations: In Japanese. Only products whose package inserts are published can be found.

resources.name: Union Register of medicinal products
resources.organization: European Commission (DG Health and Food Safety)
resources.purpose: What is the legal EU marketing authorisation status of a centrally authorised medicine, including withdrawals and suspensions?

coverage.products: Centrally authorised human and veterinary medicines, orphan medicines, referrals
coverage.reportTypes: Commission decisions and annexes; refused, withdrawn, suspended products
coverage.years: Not stated; variations not affecting the decision not shown since 1 April 2011

access.note: Browse listings; medicinal products dataset in JSON; RSS. Marked BETA.

reuse.note: Licence: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International.

resources.limitations: Shows Commission decisions, not the latest product information text; some variations are no longer reflected.

resources.name: Clinical Trials Information System (CTIS) public portal
resources.organization: European Medicines Agency with EU/EEA Member States and the European Commission
resources.purpose: What EU trials are running under the Clinical Trials Regulation, and what has been published about them?

coverage.reportTypes: Trial records under the Clinical Trials Regulation

access.note: Public search and trial map; sponsor workspaces need login.

reuse.note: Not stated on the pages checked.

resources.limitations: EMA says the site holds limited information that will grow over time; some details may be deferred to protect commercial interests or personal data.

resources.name: Clinical Trials Registry - India (CTRI)
resources.organization: ICMR National Institute for Research in Digital Health (India)
resources.purpose: What trials, BA/BE and post-marketing studies are registered in India?

coverage.countries: India (and some countries without a primary registry)
coverage.reportTypes: Trial registrations including post-marketing surveillance and BA/BE studies

access.note: Trial and advanced search; sign-in only for registrants.

reuse.note: Not stated on the page checked.

resources.limitations: Results and adverse events are not described on the registry page.

resources.name: ClinicalTrials.gov
resources.purpose: What were the results and adverse events of a registered trial?

coverage.reportTypes: Registrations and results

access.note: Not yet checked.

reuse.note: Not yet checked.

resources.limitations: Not yet checked: the site renders with JavaScript; only its API version endpoint was confirmed to answer without a key.

resources.name: EU Clinical Trials Register (EudraCT)
resources.organization: European Medicines Agency with EU/EEA national competent authorities
resources.purpose: What were the results and adverse events of an EU trial of a medicine started under the old Clinical Trials Directive?

coverage.countries: EU and EEA, plus paediatric investigation plan trials outside the EU
coverage.products: Medicines (interventional trials only; not device or surgical trials)
coverage.reportTypes: Protocols and summary results, including adverse events
coverage.years: Trials started after 1 May 2004; newer trials are in CTIS

access.note: Download up to 20 results per request as a text file.

reuse.note: Attribute 'EU Clinical Trials Register' and show the date accessed; contact emails may not be used for marketing.

resources.limitations: EMA says data entered between 2004 and March 2011 is historical and may be incomplete or inconsistent, and records may not show the current protocol status.

resources.name: ISRCTN registry
resources.purpose: What studies with UK participants are registered, and what results have they posted?

coverage.countries: Studies involving UK participants, plus others
coverage.reportTypes: Interventional and non-interventional study records, protocols, results, IPD sharing plans

access.note: All records free to search; data can be downloaded for analysis.

reuse.note: Some fields are CC BY and newer metadata CC0, but the terms also restrict copying into databases. Check the terms before bulk reuse.

resources.limitations: Content is provided by trialists and sponsors and may be out of date.

resources.name: Japan Registry of Clinical Trials (jRCT)
resources.organization: Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare (Japan)
resources.purpose: What clinical research and trials are registered in Japan?

coverage.products: Specified clinical research, other clinical research, clinical trials (chiken), regenerative medicine
coverage.reportTypes: Registered research plans published to WHO requirements

access.note: Keyword and detailed search; English pages available. The address moved to jrct.mhlw.go.jp in March 2025.

reuse.note: jRCT asks users not to collect data in bulk beyond personal use, including by automated means; see its terms of use.

resources.limitations: Mostly in Japanese; results and adverse events are not described on the top page.

resources.name: WHO International Clinical Trials Registry Platform (ICTRP)
resources.purpose: Is a trial registered anywhere in the world, across national registries?

coverage.reportTypes: Trial registrations using the WHO 24-item data set

access.note: Search portal at trialsearch.who.int; full downloads and the API web service need a request to WHO.

reuse.note: WHO terms of use: acknowledge WHO; no sale or commercial use without permission.

resources.limitations: ICTRP is not a registry itself; records come from primary registries and WHO does not warrant completeness.

resources.name: Cochrane Library
resources.purpose: What do systematic reviews conclude about the harms and benefits of an intervention?

coverage.reportTypes: Cochrane systematic reviews (CDSR), CENTRAL trial records, Cochrane Clinical Answers

access.note: Full-text access terms could not be confirmed during the check.

reuse.note: Published by Wiley; reuse generally needs permission.

resources.limitations: Reviews may be out of date; harms are often less fully reported than benefits in the trials reviewed.

resources.name: Europe PMC
resources.organization: EMBL-EBI with funders of Europe PMC
resources.purpose: Where can I search abstracts and open-access full text of safety literature, including preprints?

coverage.reportTypes: Abstracts, full-text open access articles, preprints

access.note: Not yet checked.

reuse.note: Not yet checked; depends on each article's licence.

resources.limitations: Not yet checked: the website could not be read; only its REST API was confirmed to answer without a key.

resources.name: FDA Sentinel Initiative
resources.organization: US Food and Drug Administration (Sentinel Coordinating Center)
resources.purpose: Has FDA studied a safety question in US healthcare data, and what did it find?

coverage.reportTypes: Analyses, assessments and publications from claims and electronic health record data

access.note: Analyses and reports are public; the underlying data stays with data partners and is not publicly available.

reuse.note: Not stated on the pages checked.

resources.limitations: FDA says querying a product in Sentinel does not necessarily mean there is a safety issue.

resources.name: HMA-EMA Catalogues of real-world data sources and studies
resources.organization: Heads of Medicines Agencies and European Medicines Agency
resources.purpose: Which post-authorisation and real-world studies exist for a medicine, and which data sources could answer a safety question?

coverage.reportTypes: Study and data source metadata, protocols and study reports (replaced the EU PAS Register in 2024)
coverage.years: Includes records migrated from the EU PAS Register

access.note: Searchable; records can be exported.

reuse.note: Not stated on the page checked.

resources.limitations: The completeness score measures metadata only, not the quality of the data source.

resources.name: PubMed and NCBI E-utilities
resources.organization: National Center for Biotechnology Information, US National Library of Medicine
resources.purpose: Which published studies and case reports exist on a safety question?

coverage.reportTypes: Over 40 million citations and abstracts (MEDLINE, PubMed Central, Bookshelf); not full text

access.note: Free search; E-utilities API for programmatic access.

reuse.note: The E-utilities manual is public domain; abstracts may be copyrighted by publishers. Follow NCBI usage guidelines.

resources.limitations: Citations and abstracts only; publication bias and indexing delays apply.

resources.name: AccessGUDID (Global Unique Device Identification Database)
resources.organization: US National Library of Medicine with FDA
resources.purpose: What device is behind a UDI, and what are its identification details?

coverage.countries: Devices sold in the United States
coverage.products: Medical devices with Unique Device Identifiers (about 5.2 million device identifiers)
coverage.reportTypes: Device identification records
coverage.years: Daily, weekly, monthly and full releases

access.note: Full and update downloads, RSS and REST APIs.

reuse.note: See the AccessGUDID terms of use (not checked).

resources.limitations: Identification data only, not safety reports; link to MAUDE or recalls by device identifier.

resources.name: Brighton Collaboration case definitions
resources.organization: Brighton Collaboration (a programme of The Task Force for Global Health)
resources.purpose: How should an adverse event following immunisation be defined and classified for a case assessment or study?

coverage.reportTypes: AEFI case definitions with companion guides, benefit-risk templates

access.note: Case definitions and companion guides as PDFs.

reuse.note: Site states all rights reserved; check the disclaimer before reuse.

resources.limitations: Some items are drafts open for comment; use the published version.

resources.name: Drugs and Lactation Database (LactMed)
resources.organization: US National Library of Medicine (NIH), on NCBI Bookshelf
resources.purpose: Is a medicine compatible with breastfeeding, and what is known about levels in breast milk?

coverage.reportTypes: Referenced summaries of drug levels in milk and effects on infants

access.note: Not yet checked.

reuse.note: Not yet checked.

resources.limitations: Not yet checked: the page could not be read during the automated check.

resources.name: EUDAMED (European Database on Medical Devices)
resources.organization: European Commission (DG Health and Food Safety)
resources.purpose: Which devices, manufacturers and certificates are registered in the EU?

coverage.products: Medical devices and in vitro diagnostics under Regulations 2017/745 and 2017/746
coverage.reportTypes: Actor registration, UDI and device registration, notified bodies and certificates, market surveillance (mandatory since 28 May 2026)

access.note: A public site and a restricted site; vigilance and clinical investigation modules are not yet available.

reuse.note: Not stated on the page checked.

resources.limitations: Vigilance data (incidents, field safety corrective actions) is not yet public in EUDAMED.

resources.name: FDA list of pregnancy exposure registries
resources.organization: US Food and Drug Administration (Office of Women's Health)
resources.purpose: Is there a pregnancy exposure registry for a medicine or vaccine, and whom do I contact?

coverage.countries: Mostly United States and North America
coverage.reportTypes: Registry names, conditions, sponsors and contacts (no results)

access.note: Web list with contact details for each registry.

reuse.note: Not stated on the page checked.

resources.limitations: FDA says the list may not be comprehensive, FDA does not run the registries and does not endorse them.

resources.name: FDA Medical Device Recalls database
resources.purpose: Has a medical device been recalled in the US, and what recall class was it given?

coverage.products: Medical devices, including in vitro diagnostics
coverage.reportTypes: Classified recalls; firm-initiated corrections and removals since January 2017

access.note: Search by product, code, class, date, firm or reason. Device recalls are also in openFDA.

reuse.note: Not stated on the page checked.

resources.limitations: FDA notes the posting date is when FDA classified the recall, which may be after the firm told customers.

resources.name: FDA medication errors related to CDER-regulated drugs
resources.purpose: How does FDA handle medication errors, and what has it published to prevent them?

coverage.products: Prescription, OTC, generic and biosimilar drugs regulated by CDER
coverage.reportTypes: Program description, Drug Safety Communications and articles on errors, guidance

access.note: Information page; error reports themselves are in FAERS.

reuse.note: Not stated on the page checked.

resources.limitations: Not a database. Reporting medication errors to FAERS is voluntary in the US.

resources.name: FDA Total Product Life Cycle (TPLC) database
resources.purpose: What is the whole premarket and postmarket picture for a device type: clearances, adverse events and recalls?

coverage.reportTypes: Product codes, PMAs, 510(k)s, MAUDE reports and recalls combined
coverage.years: 2011 to date in the year filter

access.note: Search by product code, regulation number and year.

reuse.note: Not stated on the page checked.

resources.limitations: Summaries by product code rather than individual devices; MAUDE cautions apply to the event counts.

resources.name: Health Canada Medical Devices Active Licence Listing (MDALL)
resources.purpose: Is a Class II, III or IV medical device licensed for sale in Canada?

coverage.products: Licensed Class II, III and IV medical devices (not Class I)
coverage.reportTypes: Active licences

access.note: Online query by company, licence, device name or identifier.

reuse.note: Canada.ca terms and conditions apply.

resources.limitations: Class I devices and devices under investigational testing or special access are not listed.

resources.name: Institute for Safe Medication Practices (ISMP, part of ECRI)
resources.purpose: What medication error alerts, lists and tools exist for safe medication practice?

coverage.reportTypes: Newsletters, alerts, error-prone lists and tools; error reporting

access.note: Newsletters and the resource library come with a paid membership; error reporting is open.

reuse.note: Copyright ECRI; see ECRI terms of service.

resources.limitations: Much content is behind a subscription; it is not a regulator.

resources.name: ISMP Canada safety bulletins
resources.organization: Institute for Safe Medication Practices Canada
resources.purpose: What medication incidents and lessons have been shared in Canada?

coverage.reportTypes: Safety bulletins and newsletters; incident reporting programmes (part of CMIRPS)

access.note: Free bulletins and newsletters with no account required.

reuse.note: Copyright ISMP Canada, all rights reserved.

resources.limitations: Bulletins describe selected incidents for learning; they are not incidence data.

resources.name: MotherToBaby fact sheets
resources.purpose: What is known about a medication or vaccine during pregnancy and breastfeeding, in plain language?

coverage.products: Medications, vaccines, substances and other exposures (275+)
coverage.reportTypes: Fact sheets in English and Spanish

access.note: Fact sheets as web pages and PDFs; free information service by phone, chat and email.

reuse.note: Fact sheets may be copied for noncommercial use without changes and with the OTIS/MTB copyright notice.

resources.limitations: General information, not a substitute for clinical advice; OTIS says content may not be peer reviewed.

resources.name: UK Teratology Information Service (UKTIS) and Bumps
resources.organization: UKTIS, commissioned by the UK Health Security Agency
resources.purpose: What is known about the safety of a medicine or vaccine in pregnancy?

coverage.products: Medicines, vaccines, chemical and radiological exposures
coverage.reportTypes: Evidence monographs for professionals; patient leaflets (Bumps)

access.note: Free leaflets and search; professional enquiry line.

reuse.note: Free reproduction for education and not-for-profit use within the NHS with acknowledgement; commercial use needs written permission.

resources.limitations: Evidence for many medicines is limited; summaries state where data are sparse.

resources.name: Vaccine Safety Datalink (VSD)
resources.organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, with US healthcare organisations
resources.purpose: Has a vaccine safety question been studied in US electronic health records, and can researchers reanalyse the data?

coverage.reportTypes: Electronic health record data and published VSD studies

access.note: Data from published studies of the past 10 years through the NCHS Research Data Center, with a proposal, IRB review, signed agreements and fees.

reuse.note: Publications must acknowledge CDC and include the required VSD disclaimer.

resources.limitations: Not a public database; access is limited to approved research on final data sets.

resources.name: WHO Global Advisory Committee on Vaccine Safety (GACVS)
resources.purpose: What has WHO's independent expert committee concluded about a vaccine safety question?

coverage.reportTypes: Committee statements and meeting reports

access.note: Statements and reports as web pages and PDFs.

reuse.note: WHO terms of use and permissions apply.

resources.limitations: Expert opinion on selected topics, not a data set; check the date of each statement.
